top_needs.title: Practice efficiency gains and ROI with DM-monitored braces and aligners versus standard recall
top_needs.brands_and_products: Damon, ormco, KLOwen, Spark, Angel, Invisalign, clearcorrect, suresmile, Lightforce, SmartSTL, ScanBox, SLB, self-ligating braces, twin brackets, damon ultima brackets, traditional fixed braces o rings
top_needs.metrics_sought: chair time reduction, appointment frequency, ROI, profitability, rentability, time saving, staff efficiency, diary changes, scheduling, appointment reduction, practice optimisation, emergencies reduction, dynamic scheduling, ongoing monitoring costs vs benefits, practice differentiation, staff satisfaction
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors are skeptical that DM will actually save time or money, or that it will meaningfully reduce appointments or improve workflow. Some believe the workflow change is not worth the effort, or that the ROI is unclear, especially for braces. Others worry about staff adaptation or increased workload.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, case study, peer-reviewed, white paper, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: How can I make DM work in a practice with 8 chairs and 15 assistants in a way that they really get the real benefits and make it work financially as well in The Netherlands?

reduced chairtime, savings and only Australian studies
top_needs.gap_assessment: Direct, high-quality comparative studies quantifying ROI and efficiency for both aligners and braces, especially in diverse practice settings, are limited. More region-specific and appliance-specific data would help address persistent skepticism.

top_needs.title: AI diagnostic accuracy and reliability of DM versus orthodontist or manual review
top_needs.metrics_sought: AI accuracy, specificity and sensitivity, reliability, accuracy of bracket debonding detection, occlusal assessment, accuracy class I goal, accuracy of AI detecting eruption, accuracy of AI versus orthodontist, accuracy of scanning, accuracy with SmartSTL, AI efficiency
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question whether DM’s AI is as accurate as a human orthodontist, especially for clinical observations, bracket debonding, or aligner tracking. Some express distrust or fear of AI, worrying about diagnostic errors or being replaced.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, peer-reviewed, white paper, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: Information on the accuracy of DM, a patient has questioned the ability of the AI to detect clinical observations
Specificity and sensitivity results for FDA application

Occlusal Assessment: A quantitative study validating the AI’s accuracy in detecting malocclusions (midline deviation, overbite, overjet, and canine relationship) found that the mean bias across all parameters was less than 0.5 mm, confirming its reliability as a remote diagnosis and triage tool.
I have a doctor who doesn't trust the accuracy of the AI.  I'd like to receive information regarding the accuracy.
how accurate is our AI?
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a need for more head-to-head studies comparing DM AI’s diagnostic performance to orthodontists, especially for specific clinical tasks and across appliances. Evidence on AI’s reliability in real-world, diverse populations is especially lacking.
